# CareerScope

> CareerScope matches job listings against a candidate's actual resume and stated
> requirements, and explains why each result scored the way it did. This public site
> lists jobs collected from supported sources and links to the original employer
> posting. The private workspace that holds resumes and profiles is a separate,
> authenticated application and is not part of this site.

## What this site is

- A read-only, static list of job postings collected from supported job sources.
- Every listing links out to the original employer or source posting to apply.
- No account, tracking or personal data is required to browse it.

## What this site is not

- It is not the CareerScope application. Resume upload, profile configuration,
  matching and saved leads live in a separate authenticated workspace that is
  deliberately excluded from search indexing.
- It does not host resumes, contact details, salary expectations or application
  history.
- It does not accept applications. Applying happens on the employer's own site.

## How matching works in the product

Matching is deterministic and explainable. A saved profile snapshot is taken when a
search starts, listings are scored against that snapshot, and each result carries the
evidence behind its score. Scores describe fit against stated requirements; they are
not predictions of hiring outcomes.

## Accuracy and limitations

- Listings reflect what the source published at collection time and can become stale.
- Salary, location and seniority are only shown when the source supplied them; missing
  values are not inferred.
- Coverage is limited to supported sources and is not a complete view of the job market.
